source_spans.locator: Psychological Review 111(1), published p.3, Abstract: children construct abstract learned representations of causal relations, described with directed graphical models

Psychological Review 111(1), PDF p.28 / published p.24, 'Inferring the Direction of Causal Relations From Interventions and Correlations': the puppet paradigm combines observations of correlations with observations of interventions to infer causal direction

Psychological Review 111(1), PDF p.31 / published p.27, Experiment 2: common-effects and association conditions match pairwise association frequencies while differing in the balance of intervention and nonintervention trials

Psychological Review 111(1), PDF p.32 / published p.28, Experiment 2 results: matched associations yield different causal-status judgments as predicted by the intervention-sensitive directed-structure account

conditions: two puppet-learning conditions have matched pairwise co-occurrence frequencies but differ in whether the critical non-co-occurrence is embedded among nonintervention trials or occurs within a sequence of intervention trials
task: observe a short sequence of puppet co-movement and non-co-movement events, then judge separately whether each puppet makes the other move
temporal_scope: pretest/training precedes the test evidence sequence, which precedes the causal-status judgments

nodes.description: matched pairwise co-occurrence and non-co-occurrence frequencies across the two test conditions
observed information about which test events were produced by an external manipulation rather than occurring without that manipulation
candidate directed relation specifying which of two simultaneous events produces the other
the child's separate judgment about whether a given puppet makes the other puppet move
matched-association comparison that varies the intervention/nonintervention status of the evidence while eliciting separate directional judgments

relations.description: the comparison holds pairwise association frequencies fixed while varying the intervention structure of the observed evidence
with pairwise association frequencies matched, children's causal-status judgments differ according to the intervention structure of the evidence
the intervention-sensitive directed-structure account uses the joint correlation and intervention pattern to select a directional structure
the structured comparison exposes whether directional judgments track intervention status rather than association frequency alone
